title: Negahmedia-co
body:
## The idea

Negahmedia needed more than a logo — it needed a visual language that could carry a growing studio across print, web and motion.

The goal was a brand system that feels confident without shouting, and stays flexible enough for very different projects.

## Designing a system, not just a mark

Instead of starting with the logo, we started with the rules: spacing, rhythm, contrast and tone of voice.

The identity was built around a small set of decisions — a restrained palette, strong typographic hierarchy and a repeatable layout grammar.

Every asset, from business cards to social templates, follows the same system.

## What shipped

- Logo and icon system
- Typography scale and color tokens
- Stationery and print templates
- Social media kit
- Studio coordinator workflows for handing assets to clients

## What I learned

A brand is not a folder of files. It is a set of decisions that survive real use.

The strongest part of this project was watching the system hold together when new people started making things with it.

title: Ofog Danesh Soraya
body:
## The idea

Ofog Danesh Soraya needed a web presence that could explain educational services clearly — and load fast on any connection.

The brief was simple: credible, calm, and easy to navigate.

## Building the site

The site was designed as a small set of reusable sections: hero, service overviews, contact and a lightweight content structure that non-technical staff can update.

Performance was treated as a feature: minimal dependencies, optimized images and a clear content hierarchy.

## What shipped

- Responsive design system
- Editorial layout for news and updates
- Contact and enrollment flows
- SEO structure and metadata

## What I learned

Educational websites succeed when they remove friction. Every screen should answer one question quickly — and get out of the way.
